description: NEAR-ZERO (tiny) hyperplane init — tests whether sparse structure EMERGES from ~nothing. IDENTICAL to exp012 (full ~325M HyperplaneMultiHeadLUT, all sites, exp752 geometry+recipe, forward 'hard', 16000 steps, hybrid Lion+AdamW routing with hyperplane params -> AdamW no-wd, seed 42) EXCEPT hyperplane_init_scale = 0.0001 (std=1e-4, near-zero) instead of exp012's 0.05. Hyperplane normals start at ~0 (biases 0 as before), so <w,x>+b ~ 0 at init — the sign tests are essentially undefined at t=0 and the hyperplanes must GROW from ~nothing. Question: does the network wake up a SPARSE set of coefficients (like exp010's anchor-init ~2-sparse geometry) or a DENSE set (like exp012's random-0.05, PR~128)? Reference finals: exp010 anchor 1.1940 (sparse geom), exp012 random-0.05 1.1953 (dense geom), exp752 fixed-anchor 1.2162, exp001 dense-MLP 1.2014. Step-0/1 loss expected ~10.56 regardless (LUT tables ~0 -> output~0). Only config diff vs exp012: hyperplane_init_scale 0.05 -> 0.0001.
